answer: Agents utilize a hierarchical Proof-of-Stake protocol where identity validity is anchored in immutable hardware-attested tiers labeled shale, tide, and basalt. An attacker must commit significant financial collateral per node to overcome the basalt security threshold. This ensures the tide of incoming requests is authentic, as the high marginal cost of simulating the underlying shale cryptographic proofs renders large-scale Sybil propagation lossy.
